current_law_statement: Researched from the owner-supplied certified source document WI_ch19_certified_2026-08-05.txt: Updated 2023-24 Wisconsin Statutes & Annotations, published August 5, 2026, certified under s. 35.18, updated through 2025 Wisconsin Act 247, including official annotations (case law and AG opinions). The history line for Wis. Stat. s. 19.35 ends at 2023 a. 253, so no 2024-2026 session law through 2025 Act 247 amended the fee section; a docs.legis.wisconsin.gov search on 2026-08-20 surfaced no later act amending s. 19.35 (SB194 is a proposal, not law). The s. 19.35(3)(h) body-camera/audio-video redaction fee regime (2023 Wis. Act 253) is in the certified text, so the prior paraphrased row WI-0041 is now amended with verbatim text (WI-9001). Guidance-vs-law gap: the widely quoted 25-cents-per-page copy figure is Wisconsin DOJ guidance on what is presumptively reasonable, NOT a statutory rate; the statute sets only an actual, necessary and direct cost standard. It is deliberately not recorded as a value anywhere in this file.

resolutions.source_language: An authority may impose a fee upon the requester of a copy of a record which may not exceed the actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction and transcription of the record, unless a fee is otherwise specifically established or authorized to be established by law.
resolutions.notes: No statutory per-page number for B&W copies; the ceiling is the 'actual, necessary and direct cost' standard. The city sets its rate under that standard. The oft-cited 25 cents/page is WI DOJ GUIDANCE on presumptive reasonableness, not law — not recorded as a value per state note. The prior_values '$50' in the input slice is a misattribution: $50 is the location-fee chargeability threshold under § 19.35(3)(c), not a copy rate. 'Authority' covers state and local bodies alike (§ 19.32(1)), so this binds municipalities.

resolutions.source_language: An authority may impose a fee upon the requester of a copy of a record which may not exceed the actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction and transcription of the record, unless a fee is otherwise specifically established or authorized to be established by law.
resolutions.notes: No separate color-copy provision anywhere in ch. 19 subch. II or its annotations; color copies fall under the same actual/necessary/direct reproduction-cost ceiling of § 19.35(3)(a). A city's color rate may reflect the higher actual cost of color reproduction but nothing more.

resolutions.source_language: An authority may impose a fee upon the requester of a copy of a record which may not exceed the actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction and transcription of the record, unless a fee is otherwise specifically established or authorized to be established by law.
resolutions.notes: No distinct oversized/nonstandard-page provision; oversized reproduction is governed by the § 19.35(3)(a) actual-cost standard (or (3)(b) photographing standard where the form does not permit copying). City sets any oversized rate under actual, necessary and direct cost.

resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law or as authorized to be prescribed by law an authority may impose a fee upon the requester of a copy of a record that does not exceed the actual, necessary and direct cost of photographing and photographic processing if the authority provides a photograph of a record, the form of which does not permit copying.
resolutions.notes: Photographs of non-copyable records: actual/necessary/direct cost of photographing and photographic processing (§ 19.35(3)(b)). Transcription is inside the (3)(a) reproduction-and-transcription standard. Record-specific fee statutes may override via the 'otherwise provided by law' clause (e.g., § 343.24(2m) for DOT accident reports — agency-specific, not municipal; Media Placement Services, Inc. v. DOT, 2018 WI App 34).

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II (ss. 19.21-19.39) including all § 19.35 annotations (case law and AG opinions 58-78 Atty. Gen. plus OAG series): no graduated/tiered per-page band provision exists.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative. Wisconsin has a pure actual-cost regime with no volume bands. A city may design tiers only insofar as each tier stays within the actual, necessary and direct cost ceiling of § 19.35(3)(a).

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II (ss. 19.21-19.39) including all § 19.35 annotations: no free-page allowance per request exists.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative. The prior slice attached WI-0033 (no fee for redaction, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel 2012 WI 65) to this item, but that is a no-charge task category, not a free-page allowance — it belongs to labor.review.rate/labor.billableWhen. The discretionary public-interest waiver (§ 19.35(3)(e)) lets a city grant free copies but sets no page number.

resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law or as authorized to be prescribed by law, an authority may impose a fee upon a requester for locating a record, not exceeding the actual, necessary and direct cost of location, if the cost is $50 or more.
resolutions.notes: No fixed hourly rate: location (search) labor is charged at actual, necessary and direct cost, and ONLY when that cost is $50 or more (chargeability threshold resolved at labor.billableWhen). DOJ guidance says the staff-time rate should be based on the lowest-paid employee capable of the task (guidance, not statute, for general location; the lowest-paid-employee rate IS statutory for § 19.35(3)(h)6 A/V redaction). Prior '$10,000' value in the slice is the false-certification forfeiture of (3)(h)3.a, not a labor rate.

resolutions.source_authority: Milwaukee Journal Sentinel v. City of Milwaukee, 2012 WI 65, 341 Wis. 2d 607, 815 N.W.2d 367; Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3)(h)
resolutions.source_language: Under sub. (3) (a) to (d), 2011 stats., the legislature provided four tasks for which an authority may impose fees on a requester: 1) reproduction and transcription; 2) photographing and photographic processing; 3) locating; and 4) mailing or shipping. For each task, an authority is permitted to impose a fee that does not exceed the actual, necessary, and direct cost of the task. The process of redacting information from a record does not fit into any of those four statutory tasks.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (certified through 2025 Wis. Act 247, published 2026-08-05); modified for law-enforcement A/V only by 2023 Wis. Act 253
resolutions.notes: Review/redaction labor is categorically non-chargeable for general records, so a review labor rate is moot — fee is $0. SOLE exception: a law enforcement agency redacting recorded audio/video under § 19.35(3)(h) (verbatim now captured in WI-9001, amending the previously paraphrased WI-0041): actual/necessary/direct cost, staff-time rate statutorily pinned to the pay rate of the authority's lowest paid employee capable of performing the task ((3)(h)6), subject to the (3)(h)3-5 no-charge categories and the (3)(h)7 written-estimate precondition. Verbatim quote is from the official annotation in the certified statutes.

resolutions.source_language: Copying fees, but not location fees, may be imposed on a requester for the cost of a computer run. 72 Atty. Gen. 68.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (annotation carried in certified 2023-24 statutes published 2026-08-05)
resolutions.manual_verification: Verbatim is the official annotation line in the certified statutes, not the opinion body; the underlying 72 Atty. Gen. 68 opinion was not separately opened. Confirm scope if a city wants to charge programming as 'reproduction'.
resolutions.notes: No programming rate exists. The cost of a computer run is chargeable as a copying (reproduction) fee under the § 19.35(3)(a) actual-cost standard — not as a location fee (so the $50 location threshold does not attach to it). Note also § 19.35(1)(L): no duty to create a new record by extracting and compiling information into a new format (except (1)(c)-(e) and § 19.36(6)), which bounds when programming work is owed at all.

resolutions.unit: USD (location-cost chargeability threshold: location/search labor chargeable only if its actual cost is $50 or more)
resolutions.source_authority: Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3)(c); Milwaukee Journal Sentinel v. City of Milwaukee, 2012 WI 65; Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3)(h)
resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law or as authorized to be prescribed by law, an authority may impose a fee upon a requester for locating a record, not exceeding the actual, necessary and direct cost of location, if the cost is $50 or more.
resolutions.notes: Engine shape: (1) location/search labor: chargeable only when the location cost reaches $50 (below $50 it is free, and per WI-0037 notes sub-$50 location costs may not be folded into reproduction charges); (2) review/redaction labor: never chargeable for general records (Milwaukee Journal Sentinel); (3) LE audio/video redaction labor: chargeable only under the § 19.35(3)(h) conditions (non-commercial individual certification + ≤10 A/V requests/yr exempts; involved parties and officer-involved shootings always exempt; written estimate required first). No paper-only limitation appears anywhere. The $50 figure is the only fixed number in the general labor regime.

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no overhead or fringe-benefit surcharge percentage exists.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative. No overhead multiplier is authorized. The statutory standard is 'actual, necessary and DIRECT cost' — the word 'direct' cuts against loading indirect/overhead costs onto any fee, though the statute does not expressly address a percentage. A city should not configure an overhead percentage in Wisconsin.

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no labor time increment or rounding rule exists.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative. Any billing increment a city adopts must still keep the resulting charge within actual, necessary and direct cost (§ 19.35(3)(a)-(c)); an increment that systematically overshoots actual cost would exceed the ceiling.

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no free-labor-hours-per-request allowance exists.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative. Wisconsin's functional analogue is a COST threshold, not an hours threshold: location labor is free until its cost reaches $50 (§ 19.35(3)(c), resolved at labor.billableWhen). Do not convert $50 into an hours figure.

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no per-requestor periodic free personnel time allowance (TX § 552.275 pattern) exists.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative. The only per-requestor periodic counter in Wisconsin law is the § 19.35(3)(h)3.b 10-requests-per-calendar-year threshold gating the LE A/V redaction fee (see repeat item) — it counts requests, not free hours.

resolutions.source_authority: Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3) (searched; general regime has no provision); cf. § 19.35(3)(h)7
resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no general itemized-estimate or cost-notice threshold exists. Narrow exception verbatim: An authority may not impose the fee under subd. 2. with respect to a request for records containing audio or video content unless prior to fulfilling the request the authority provides to the requester in writing an estimate of the amount of the fee to be charged.
resolutions.notes: General regime: silent — no dollar/hours threshold triggering a mandatory estimate. One narrow statutory estimate gate exists: § 19.35(3)(h)7 makes a prior WRITTEN estimate a precondition of charging the LE A/V redaction fee (any amount — no threshold; captured in WI-9001). DOJ guidance encourages estimates generally, but that is guidance, not law.

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no requester response window for estimates (nor any deemed-withdrawal on estimate non-response) exists.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative. Defers in practice to city policy; state law is silent.

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no revised-estimate-on-variance percentage exists.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative. The final charge is independently capped at actual, necessary and direct cost regardless of any estimate.

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no estimate validity period exists.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative. Defers in practice to city policy.

resolutions.unit: USD (prepayment may be required only if total fees exceed $5)
resolutions.source_language: An authority may require prepayment by a requester of any fee or fees imposed under this subsection if the total amount exceeds $5.
resolutions.notes: Fixed statutory threshold: prepayment (Wisconsin's deposit mechanism) is permitted only when total fees EXCEED $5; demanding prepayment of $1.29 on a mail request was unlawful (State ex rel. Borzych v. Paluszcyk, 201 Wis. 2d 523 — confirmed in certified annotations). Amount demanded may rest on a reasonable estimate (Hill v. Zimmerman, WI-0044). Permission, not requirement — the city decides whether to demand prepayment above the threshold.

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no percentage cap on prepayment exists.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative. § 19.35(3)(f) permits prepayment of 'any fee or fees' — i.e., up to 100% of the (reasonably estimated) total; no statutory percentage ceiling below that.

resolutions.source_authority: Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3)(f); § 19.35(1)(i); State ex rel. Hill v. Zimmerman, 196 Wis. 2d 419
resolutions.source_language: An authority may require prepayment by a requester of any fee or fees imposed under this subsection if the total amount exceeds $5. [§ 19.35(1)(i):] Except as authorized under this paragraph, no request under pars. (a) to (f) may be refused because the request is received by mail, unless prepayment of a fee is required under sub. (3) (f).
resolutions.notes: Shape of the gate: production MAY be conditioned on payment in advance when total fees exceed $5 (prepay-before-copies); the prepayment amount may be based on a reasonable estimate (Hill v. Zimmerman). § 19.35(1)(i) expressly recognizes withholding fulfillment of a mail request pending required prepayment. Below the $5 threshold, production may not be conditioned on advance payment (Borzych). Discretionary — city configures whether to use the gate.

resolutions.source_language: If the requester is a prisoner, as defined in s. 301.01 (2), or is a person confined in a federal correctional institution located in this state, and he or she has failed to pay any fee that was imposed by the authority for a request made previously by that requester, the authority may require prepayment both of the amount owed for the previous request and the amount owed for the current request.
resolutions.notes: The only statutory nonpayment consequence is the prior-debt prepayment rule, and it is limited to prisoner requesters: unpaid fees from a previous request let the authority demand prepayment of BOTH the old and the new amounts before fulfilling the current request. There is NO general deemed-withdrawal-after-N-days rule for unpaid fees or estimates — that half of the item is silent and falls to city policy.

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no provision states the effect of an unpaid prepayment demand on the response obligation, no grace period, and no lapse action.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative — and there is no numeric statutory clock to toll in the first place: § 19.35(4)(a) requires action 'as soon as practicable and without delay' (a soft standard). Practically, § 19.35(1)(i) + (3)(f) let the authority hold fulfillment until a lawful prepayment demand is met, but no statute assigns a grace period or lapse action; those are city policy.

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no overrun/re-issue rule (revised estimate requirement, collection block, or window restart) exists for the general regime.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative. The narrow § 19.35(3)(h)7 written-estimate rule is a precondition of charging the LE A/V redaction fee at all, not an overrun/re-issue mechanism. The actual-cost ceiling independently caps the final charge whatever was estimated.
out of scope per owner decision 2026-08-20 — finance-department policy, excluded from state rules profile

resolutions.source_authority: Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3)(a)-(d); Milwaukee Journal Sentinel v. City of Milwaukee, 2012 WI 65
resolutions.source_language: Under sub. (3) (a) to (d), 2011 stats., the legislature provided four tasks for which an authority may impose fees on a requester: 1) reproduction and transcription; 2) photographing and photographic processing; 3) locating; and 4) mailing or shipping. For each task, an authority is permitted to impose a fee that does not exceed the actual, necessary, and direct cost of the task.
resolutions.notes: Request-level ceiling is structural, not numeric: total charge = sum of actual, necessary and direct cost of the enumerated chargeable tasks (reproduction/transcription, photographing/processing, location if ≥$50, mailing/shipping, plus LE A/V redaction under (3)(h)) and nothing else. Enforcement backstop: arbitrary/capricious excessive fees expose the authority to punitive damages and a forfeiture up to $1,000 (§ 19.37(3)-(4)) — remedy amounts noted only, per keeper-sliver rule. Contractor-produced records carry the contractor-cost cap (§ 19.35(3)(g), WI-0040).

resolutions.source_authority: Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3) (searched; no general de-minimis provision)
resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no general no-charge-below-$X (de minimis) rule exists.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative for a REQUEST-LEVEL de minimis. Two task-scoped analogues exist and are resolved elsewhere: location fees are barred below $50 of location cost (§ 19.35(3)(c), labor.billableWhen) and prepayment is barred at $5 or less (§ 19.35(3)(f), rules.deposit.threshold). A city MAY waive small charges under the discretionary public-interest waiver (§ 19.35(3)(e), WI-0039) but the state sets no de-minimis dollar figure.

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no minimum fee exists.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative. A flat minimum fee that exceeds actual, necessary and direct cost on a small request would violate the § 19.35(3)(a) ceiling — do not configure one for Wisconsin.

resolutions.source_language: An authority may impose a fee upon the requester of a copy of a record which may not exceed the actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction and transcription of the record, unless a fee is otherwise specifically established or authorized to be established by law.
resolutions.manual_verification: No provision names CD/DVD/USB; treating the physical medium as part of the actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction is a scope judgment (consistent with 72 Atty. Gen. 68 treating computer-run costs as copying costs).
resolutions.notes: No statutory media price. The actual cost of the storage medium used to deliver the copy is chargeable under the § 19.35(3)(a) reproduction standard; nothing beyond actual cost. Electronic-form requests must be answered in electronic form (Lueders v. Krug, 2019 WI App 36 — in certified annotations), so a paper surcharge cannot be forced instead.

resolutions.source_language: An authority may impose a fee upon a requester for the actual, necessary and direct cost of mailing or shipping of any copy or photograph of a record which is mailed or shipped to the requester.
resolutions.notes: Mailing/shipping chargeable at actual, necessary and direct cost. No statute authorizes a handling surcharge, an email-delivery charge, or a pickup charge — mailing/shipping is one of only four (now five with (3)(h)) chargeable tasks (Milwaukee Journal Sentinel), so email delivery and pickup carry no delivery fee.

resolutions.source_language: A custodian may not require a requester to pay the cost of an unrequested certification. Unless the fee for copies of records is established by law, a custodian may not charge more than the actual and direct cost of reproduction. 72 Atty. Gen. 36.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (annotation carried in certified 2023-24 statutes published 2026-08-05)
resolutions.manual_verification: Verbatim is the official annotation line; underlying 72 Atty. Gen. 36 opinion body not separately opened. Record-specific certification fee statutes (e.g., vital records, clerk fee schedules) exist outside the records law and were not inventoried — out of this pass's scope.
resolutions.notes: The records law sets NO certification rate. Operative rule is a gate: an UNREQUESTED certification may not be charged to the requester (WI-9003). A requested certification's charge, if any, comes from a record-specific fee statute (via the § 19.35(3)(a) 'otherwise established by law' clause) or stays within actual cost; there is no general records-law certification fee for a city to configure.

resolutions.source_language: Subject to subds. 3. to 7., an authority that is a law enforcement agency may impose a fee upon a requester for the actual, necessary, and direct cost of redacting, whether by pixelization or other means, recorded audio or video content to the extent redaction is necessary to comply with applicable constitutional, statutory, or common law.
resolutions.notes: No per-recording, per-minute, or free-minutes values anywhere. Copies of audio ((1)(c)) and video ((1)(d)) records are charged as reproduction at actual, necessary and direct cost ((3)(a)). Law enforcement agencies (including municipal police) may additionally charge actual A/V REDACTION cost under (3)(h) — staff rate pinned to lowest-paid capable employee, barred for involved individuals/representatives, officer-involved shootings, and non-commercial individual requesters with ≤10 A/V requests that calendar year, and conditioned on a prior written estimate (WI-9001).

resolutions.source_authority: Wis. Stat. § 19.35 (searched; no general commercial schedule); cf. § 19.35(3)(h)3.a
resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including all § 19.35 annotations: no commercial-purpose fee schedule or surcharge exists. Purpose may generally not be demanded: Except as authorized under this paragraph, no request under pars. (a) and (b) to (f) may be refused because the person making the request is unwilling to be identified or to state the purpose of the request.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative for a commercial schedule; § 19.35(1)(i) generally bars conditioning access on stated purpose (and examination of records cannot be denied for commercial purpose, 58 Atty. Gen. 67). ONE commercial-sensitive fork exists: under § 19.35(3)(h)3.a an individual requester escapes the LE A/V redaction fee by certifying no use for financial gain ($10,000 forfeiture per false certification) — i.e., commercially-purposed requesters can be charged that one fee where others cannot. Captured in WI-9001.

resolutions.source_authority: Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3)(e); George v. Record Custodian, 169 Wis. 2d 573, 485 N.W.2d 460 (Ct. App. 1992)
resolutions.source_language: An authority may provide copies of a record without charge or at a reduced charge where the authority determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest.
resolutions.notes: Shape: single DISCRETIONARY waiver/reduction branch, sole statutory ground = authority's own public-interest determination. No mandatory waiver categories; no indigency waiver as of right (George v. Record Custodian, verbatim in WI-9004); no purpose-statement requirement (indeed § 19.35(1)(i) generally bars demanding purpose); no waiver-specific written-denial or appeal procedure (general denial machinery of § 19.35(4)(b)/§ 19.37 applies to record denials, not fee-waiver refusals).

resolutions.source_language: Searched certified Wis. Stat. ch. 19 subch. II including §§ 19.35 and 19.37 and all annotations: no rule forfeits or waives the fee itself when the authority responds late.
resolutions.notes: Structured negative. Do not confuse with § 19.37(4): the up-to-$1,000 forfeiture for arbitrary/capricious delay or excessive fees is a penalty paid to the state/county via AG/DA enforcement, not a waiver of the requester's fee. Wisconsin also has no fixed response deadline ('as soon as practicable and without delay') for a late-response trigger to hang on.

resolutions.source_language: b. During the calendar year in which the authority receives the request, the same requester has not made more than 10 requests to the authority for records containing audio or video content, including the current request but excluding any request subject to subd. 4. or 5.
resolutions.notes: General repeat/aggregation regime: silent — no fee carry-forward and no request-aggregation threshold for ordinary records. The one statutory per-requestor counter is § 19.35(3)(h)3.b: a requester-ledger of audio/video requests per authority per calendar year; at more than 10 such requests, the non-commercial-certification shield lapses and the LE A/V redaction fee becomes chargeable (requests by involved parties (subd. 4) and officer-involved-shooting requests (subd. 5) are excluded from the count). Engine needs a per-requestor-per-authority-per-calendar-year A/V request counter for law-enforcement bodies. Applies to any authority that is a law enforcement agency, including municipal police.

new_rules.legal_concept: Law enforcement audio/video redaction fee (verbatim, certified text)
new_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of redacting recorded audio/video content; staff rate = pay rate of the authority's lowest paid employee capable of performing the task
new_rules.atomic_rule: A law enforcement agency may impose a fee for the actual, necessary and direct cost of redacting recorded audio or video content to the extent redaction is legally required; the fee is barred where an individual requester certifies non-financial-gain use AND has made no more than 10 A/V requests to that authority that calendar year, where the requester is directly involved in the event (or their attorney/representative/parent/guardian), or where the event is an officer-involved shooting; the staff-time rate must be based on the lowest-paid capable employee; and no fee may be imposed unless a written estimate was provided before fulfilling the request.
new_rules.trigger: A law enforcement agency redacts recorded audio or video content to respond to a request
new_rules.source_language: 2. Subject to subds. 3. to 7., an authority that is a law enforcement agency may impose a fee upon a requester for the actual, necessary, and direct cost of redacting, whether by pixelization or other means, recorded audio or video content to the extent redaction is necessary to comply with applicable constitutional, statutory, or common law. 3. An authority may not impose the fee under subd. 2. with respect to a request for records containing audio or video content for which all of the following apply: a. If the requester is an individual, the requester provides written certification to the authority that the requester will not use the audio or video content for financial gain, not including an award of damages in a civil action. Any individual providing a false certification under this subd. 3. a. shall be subject to a forfeiture of $10,000 for each violation. b. During the calendar year in which the authority receives the request, the same requester has not made more than 10 requests to the authority for records containing audio or video content, including the current request but excluding any request subject to subd. 4. or 5. 4. An authority may not impose the fee under subd. 2. with respect to a request for records containing audio or video content if the requester is an individual directly involved in the event to which the requested records relate, that individual’s attorney or other authorized representative, or that individual’s parent or guardian if the individual is under the age of 18. 5. An authority may not impose the fee under subd. 2. with respect to a request for records containing audio or video content if the event to which the requested records relate is a shooting involving an officer of a law enforcement agency. 6. In calculating the fee imposed under subd. 2., the rate for an actual, necessary, and direct charge for staff time spent redacting shall be based on the pay rate of the authority’s lowest paid employee capable of performing the task. 7. An authority may not impose the fee under subd. 2. with respect to a request for records containing audio or video content unless prior to fulfilling the request the authority provides to the requester in writing an estimate of the amount of the fee to be charged.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (certified 2023-24 Wisconsin Statutes through 2025 Wis. Act 247, published 2026-08-05)
new_rules.notes: AMENDS WI-0041, which was is_paraphrase=true and flagged for manual verification of exact text and effective status: the certified statutes (published 2026-08-05, through 2025 Act 247) resolve both. Text is codified and current; § 19.35 history line ends at 2023 a. 253. Narrow exception to WI-0033's general no-redaction-fee rule. 'Law enforcement agency' per § 19.36(8)(a)2. ((3)(h)1.), which includes municipal police.

new_rules.legal_concept: Computer-run cost chargeable as copying fee, not location fee
new_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction (computer-run cost treated as copying)
new_rules.atomic_rule: The cost of a computer run may be imposed on a requester as a copying fee, but not as a location fee.
new_rules.trigger: Responding to a request requires a computer run
new_rules.source_language: Copying fees, but not location fees, may be imposed on a requester for the cost of a computer run. 72 Atty. Gen. 68.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (annotation carried in certified 2023-24 statutes published 2026-08-05)
new_rules.notes: Verbatim from the official annotation to § 19.35 in the certified statutes; the opinion body itself was not separately opened. Consequence: the $50 location-fee threshold of § 19.35(3)(c) does not gate computer-run charges, but the § 19.35(3)(a) actual-cost ceiling does. See also § 19.35(1)(L) (no duty to create new records) bounding when such work is owed.

new_rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may not require a requester to pay the cost of a certification the requester did not ask for; and unless a copy fee is established by law, the custodian may not charge more than the actual and direct cost of reproduction.
new_rules.trigger: Custodian certifies a copy the requester did not request certified
new_rules.source_language: A custodian may not require a requester to pay the cost of an unrequested certification. Unless the fee for copies of records is established by law, a custodian may not charge more than the actual and direct cost of reproduction. 72 Atty. Gen. 36.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (annotation carried in certified 2023-24 statutes published 2026-08-05)
new_rules.notes: Verbatim from the official annotation to § 19.35 in the certified statutes; opinion body not separately opened. The records law sets no certification rate; record-specific statutes may (via the § 19.35(3)(a) 'otherwise established by law' clause).

new_rules.legal_concept: No indigency fee exemption as of right
new_rules.atomic_rule: The public records law confers no exemption as of right on indigent requesters from payment of fees under § 19.35(3); any fee relief for indigents is only through the discretionary public-interest waiver.
new_rules.source_language: The public records law confers no exemption as of right on indigents from payment of fees under sub. (3). George v. Record Custodian, 169 Wis. 2d 573, 485 N.W.2d 460 (Ct. App. 1992).
new_rules.source_authority: George v. Record Custodian, 169 Wis. 2d 573, 485 N.W.2d 460 (Ct. App. 1992)
new_rules.effective_status: Current (annotation carried in certified 2023-24 statutes published 2026-08-05)
new_rules.notes: Verbatim from the official annotation to § 19.35 in the certified statutes. Secondary rule type: Discretion (relief remains available under § 19.35(3)(e) at the authority's option). Previously carried only as a note on WI-0039; promoted to a row because it is operative for the waiver item (no mandatory indigency ground).

delegations_followed.statute_cite: Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3)(a) ('unless a fee is otherwise specifically established or authorized to be established by law')
delegations_followed.instrument: Record-specific fee statutes outside the records law (savings clause, not a delegation to a rule-making body)
delegations_followed.instrument_cite: Example confirmed in certified annotations: Wis. Stat. § 343.24(2m) (DOT accident-report inspection fees; Media Placement Services, Inc. v. DOT, 2018 WI App 34)
delegations_followed.figures_extracted: None — the clause points to scattered record-specific statutes, not to any uniform fee schedule; the confirmed example (DOT) is agency-specific and does not bind municipalities. No administrative rule, AG rule, or uniform schedule holds a municipal records fee figure in Wisconsin, and no statute delegates municipal records fees to any instrument (an agency cannot create records-law exceptions by rule: Chvala v. Bubolz, 204 Wis. 2d 82).

applicability_notes: Wisconsin runs ONE fee regime for all 'authorities' (Wis. Stat. § 19.32(1) covers state and local bodies alike), so every § 19.35(3) figure and standard binds municipalities directly; there is no separate state-agency uniform fee schedule and no municipal carve-out.

The § 19.35(3)(h) audio/video redaction fee applies only to authorities that are law enforcement agencies (§ 19.36(8)(a)2.), which includes municipal police departments; for a city's non-police records it is irrelevant.

The widely quoted 25 cents/page copy figure is Wisconsin DOJ guidance on presumptive reasonableness under the actual-cost standard — guidance, not law; deliberately recorded nowhere as a value in this file.

Record-specific fee statutes (vital records, clerk schedules, DOT § 343.24(2m), etc.) can displace § 19.35(3)(a) via its 'otherwise established by law' clause; these are record-specific overlays, not the municipal default regime, and were not inventoried in this pass.
material_negatives: No statutory per-page copy rate (B&W or color) — only the actual, necessary and direct cost ceiling; the 25-cent figure is DOJ guidance only.
No graduated page bands, free-page allowance, free labor hours, periodic free personnel time, minimum fee, or general de-minimis threshold.
No overhead/fringe surcharge and no labor time-increment rule; 'direct cost' language cuts against overhead loading.

No general estimate machinery: no notice threshold, requester response window, revision-on-variance percentage, validity period, or overrun re-issue rule (sole exception: the § 19.35(3)(h)7 written-estimate precondition for the LE A/V redaction fee).
No deposit percentage cap; no statutory clock/grace/lapse mechanics for unpaid prepayment (and no numeric response clock at all — 'as soon as practicable').
No general nonpayment deemed-withdrawal rule (prisoner prior-debt prepayment is the only statutory nonpayment consequence).
No commercial-purpose fee schedule; purpose generally may not be demanded (§ 19.35(1)(i)).
No fee forfeiture on late response (§ 19.37(4)'s $1,000 forfeiture is a state-enforced penalty, not fee relief).
No mandatory fee-waiver grounds — waiver is purely discretionary (public interest), and indigency confers no exemption as of right (George).
Redaction/review labor is categorically non-chargeable for general records (Milwaukee Journal Sentinel 2012 WI 65) — a material negative most states' configurations would get wrong.
gaps_manual_verification: labor.programming.rate / WI-9002 and certification / WI-9003: verbatim text is the official annotation line in the certified statutes; the underlying opinion bodies (72 Atty. Gen. 68 and 72 Atty. Gen. 36) were not separately opened.
media: treating the physical medium (CD/DVD/USB) as part of actual reproduction cost is a scope judgment — no provision names media.
Record-specific certification/copy fee statutes outside ch. 19 (vital records, municipal clerk schedules) were not inventoried; a city relying on one should verify it independently.
Session laws enacted after 2025 Wis. Act 247 (post 2026-08-05 certification) are not reflected; a docs.legis search on 2026-08-20 found none amending § 19.35.
